proposals.title: Compare the observed result with its expectation
proposals.description: An expected-result sheet aligns over an observed-result sheet for each authored test. Matching wording registers exactly, mismatches separate into a visible gap, and unobserved results remain untested.
proposals.creativeDirection: Frames 12..42 reveal up to three test stations with short input captions. Frames 43..108 register the expected translucent strip over each observed strip, matching their fixed left edges. For lower, translate it vertically into place. For hinge, rotate it around its fixed upper edge and settle it flat before judging equality. Equal strings register into a double outline. Unequal strings separate vertically and retain both complete values with a mismatch bracket. A null observation retains an empty lower slot and never receives a verdict. Frames 109..167 hold all tests, expected results, observations and derived states together. Use deterministic frame-driven React/SVG at 960x600, 180 frames and 30 fps, with the shared palette. Reveal during frames 0..11 and fade to the common opaque ground during frames 168..179.
goodFor: Explain the role of a test oracle
Show an adversarial test without claiming a comprehensive audit
Distinguish missing test evidence from a failed test
proposals.intent: Make a test judgment inspectable through its expected and observed values.

inputs.constraints: 1..3 cases; unique IDs 1..20 characters; label and inputLabel 1..24 characters; expected and non-null observed 1..20 characters; exact case-sensitive string equality defines match; null means unobserved, never failure.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Visible comparison states.
inputs.constraints: Each value 1..22 characters.

inputs.description: How the expected sheet registers with its observation.
inputs.constraints: Presentation only; both modes use identical case comparisons.

inputs.description: Keep the short input cue visible during comparison.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; hiding it does not change results.

inputs.description: Add a distinct outline, mismatch bracket or question marker beside the text state.
inputs.constraints: Boolean; state wording always remains visible.

inputs.name: exampleLabel
inputs.description: Persistent evidence qualifier.
inputs.constraints: 1..48 characters.

bindingExample.shortSourceText: A fictional ticket checker is expected to admit Ticket A and hold expired Ticket B. The observed checker admits both, exposing one mismatch.

proposals.distinction: Unlike capability-matrix, test states are derived from explicit expected and observed values rather than entered as capability claims. Unlike scan-lines, the animation exposes the comparison oracle and retains the discrepant result.
limits: No software or model is executed. The cases and observations are authored examples.
A finite set of matches does not establish safety, reliability, quality, or complete test coverage.
String equality is the only comparison. No semantic equivalence, tolerance, hidden normalization, or causal diagnosis is inferred.
proposals.verificationFocus: Changing an observation from the expected string to a different string changes only that case to mismatch. Setting it to null produces an unobserved slot with no pass or fail.

sourceRefs.rationale: The source connects dependable tools to consequential work and calls for extensive testing and adversarial model review.

Frames 77..130 place it in the deferred tray or the supplied empty work slot. Frames 131..167 hold the unchanged protected blocks, retained commitments and visible request disposition. proposals.title: Fix the source after containing the leak
proposals.description: A worker first contains a recurring leak, then repairs its source and performs one supplied retest. Temporary containment and prevention remain visibly different actions.

Frames 63..106 pause the flow and let the worker apply the authored joint repair. Frames 107..140 restore the normal outlet flow only when a retest exists, showing either no side leak or a continued side leak according to the supplied result. For not-tested, retain the paused flow and an untested tag. Frames 141..167 hold the catch tray, repaired joint and explicit observation. The normal outlet must still run for a stopped-leak result so closing the supply cannot masquerade as prevention. Use deterministic frame-driven React/SVG at 960x600, 180 frames and 30 fps, with the shared palette. Reveal during frames 0..11 and fade to the common opaque ground during frames 168..179.
goodFor: Distinguish immediate relief from recurring-cause repair

proposals.title: Deliver with the remaining repair obligations visible
proposals.description: An artifact may move to a recipient only when no open blocking issue remains. Every open follow-up issue stays attached as a visible limitation and creates an owned, dated repair obligation.
proposals.creativeDirection: Frames 12..40 reveal an artifact with its authored issue tabs and an empty repair register. Frames 41..90 unfold each open follow-up tab into a matching register entry with its owner and due label, leaving the original limitation attached to the artifact. Resolved issues keep a resolved mark. Frames 91..130 move the artifact to the recipient only if every blocking issue is resolved. Otherwise keep it behind a held bracket. Frames 131..167 hold the actual artifact location and all unresolved obligations. A due label is a commitment, never a completed repair. Use deterministic frame-driven React/SVG at 960x600, 180 frames and 30 fps, with the shared palette. Reveal during frames 0..11 and fade to the common opaque ground during frames 168..179.
goodFor: Explain a bounded release without erasing known limitations
Keep technical debt ownership visible after delivery
Distinguish an open blocker from an explicitly deferred follow-up
proposals.intent: Separate delivery from the continuing duty to address known flaws.

proposals.distinction: Unlike readiness-latch, the result may move while explicitly classified follow-up obligations remain open. Unlike feedback-refinement, delivery does not imply a finished revision cycle; unresolved work retains identity, an owner and a due label.

proposals.title: Prepare one guide that the whole team can reuse

Frames 49..130 carry that same guide to each collaborator in input order. At each station the collaborator aligns the guide with their existing blank workpiece and makes the matching marks, then releases the unchanged guide for the next person. Frames 131..167 hold all separate marked workpieces and the retained guide together. Do not turn the guide into copies of itself or show a numeric acceleration. Use deterministic frame-driven React/SVG at 960x600, 180 frames and 30 fps, with the shared palette. Reveal during frames 0..11 and fade to the common opaque ground during frames 168..179.
goodFor: Explain preparatory work that supports teammates
Show a reusable method applied to distinct outputs
Distinguish shared enablement from an individual speed claim
proposals.intent: Make the benefit of shared preparation concrete without inventing a performance multiplier.

proposals.title: Take the work to another tool
proposals.description: A person packs copies of their work into a portable folio and brings it to another workbench. Artifact identities survive the transfer, and the original work remains visible at the source.

Frames 43..92 lift one labeled copy of each artifact into a single portable folio while originals stay anchored in place. Frames 93..130 let the owner carry the folio to the destination. For accepted, open it and place each same-ID copy on the destination surface. For awaiting-open, retain the closed folio without a success mark. Frames 131..167 hold both tool labels, the owner and the actual transfer state. Do not animate format conversion or infer compatibility. Use deterministic frame-driven React/SVG at 960x600, 180 frames and 30 fps, with the shared palette. Reveal during frames 0..11 and fade to the common opaque ground during frames 168..179.

proposals.title: Change one part through a designed seam
proposals.description: A modular enclosure exposes one replaceable panel. A worker removes and replaces only that part while the surrounding modules retain their positions, labels and identities.
proposals.creativeDirection: Frames 12..42 reveal a single enclosure with a bounded row of modules. Frames 43..78 open a service latch around the targeted module and expose its existing connector. Frames 79..116 withdraw that module into a retained-parts tray, seat the supplied replacement on the same connector and close the latch. Frames 117..167 hold the changed module, unchanged neighbors and removed original together. Never dissolve or rebuild the enclosure to suggest local maintainability. Use deterministic frame-driven React/SVG at 960x600, 180 frames and 30 fps, with the shared palette. Reveal during frames 0..11 and fade to the common opaque ground during frames 168..179.

limitations: All 10 PDF pages were extracted with Poppler and visually inspected at page level. The PDF is a values statement, not verification of implemented product behavior, labor policies in force or measured business results.

Company names, private financial circumstances, exact policy quantities, claimed crisis outcomes and asserted productivity multipliers are omitted from stock examples. Defaults are invented bounded examples and are explicitly labeled fictional.
The physical jig, leak, modular enclosure and portable folio are original explanatory metaphors inferred from stated principles. They are not literal workflows documented in the source.

The values document names technical excellence and creative architecture without specifying algorithms, statistical methods or detailed system internals. Those gaps are not filled from general knowledge.
The company profile was loaded only to satisfy the source repository's context rule. No profile numbers, feature claims or policies were used as proposal evidence.

No source files were changed and no source content was uploaded externally. The source skill requests brain cleanup after retrieval, but the task's explicit read-only source constraint takes precedence; no cleanup mutation was run.
